knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Painting over damp or staining hides the cause. The cause must be found and recorded, and the surface dried, before painting.
Older surfaces may contain lead or asbestos. Disturbing them before assessment is not acceptable.
The Victorian source records the 10 square metre and one hour in any seven days limit for non-friable asbestos (asbestos.vic.gov.au page, no date shown). The limit does not apply to friable asbestos.
The patch and prime section says filler suits shallow gaps in painted surfaces, and that deeper repairs may need a different material.

practicalCriteria: Given a simulated wall with a stain and flaking paint, the worker records the moisture finding and does not paint until the cause is recorded.
The worker selects a primer and patch material for a stated substrate and states the reason.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Surface condition record for the simulated wall
stopWorkCriteria: Damp or active staining is present and the cause is not known
The surface may contain lead or asbestos and has not been assessed
